newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay bourse to challenge rival with expansion.
newsitem.headline: Bombay bourse to challenge rival with expansion.

text.p: India's oldest bourse, the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), expects to double its turnover and challenge the leadership of its rival by going on-line across the country.
"It's a niche area for us. I expect a quantum jump in business," Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) President Madan Gopal Damani told Reuters on Friday.
Market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) on Thursday approved the BSE's proposal to expand its on-line trading system from just one centre to 99 nationwide.
Damani said the expansion would immediately add four billion rupees to the BSE's current average daily turnover of 9-10 billion rupees, and then double it in three months.
"We hope to reach every investor in their home ground," he said. "We want to make investors as comfortable as possible."
The BSE is awaiting approval from the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) for satellite link-up facilities to enable the expansion.
"If DoT's clearance comes today, all the 99 centres will be operational in a week's time," Damani said, adding that the DoT had promised to approve the plan this week.
He said the BSE had already set up 137 trading terminals in the 99 centres and trial runs at some locations just outside Bombay had been successfully completed.
The expansion would put the 122-year-old exchange in direct competition with the National Stock Exchange (NSE), the country's youngest.
The NSE operates from 156 centres across India and had an average daily turnover of 18.58 billion rupees in June.
Damani said the BSE, which presently operates only from Bombay, offered a wider range of stocks to investors.
NSE figures show that 10 shares accounted for 85 percent of its daily turnover. On the BSE, Damani says, 100 shares contributed to 95 percent of daily business.
There are 569 shares listed on the NSE and it permits trading in another 927. About 1,250 different shares are traded on the exchange everyday.
The BSE has about 5,800 shares listed, of which about 2,200 are traded daily and some 2,500 traded every week, Damani said.

The BSE has also tied up with regional exchanges in Calcutta and Ahmedabad -- and will sign an agreement on Saturday with the Pune bourse in western Maharashtra -- to set up BSE's trading terminals in those centres, he said.
"We hope to expand to another 100 centres in two months," he added.
